style: Say in a knowledgeable, friendly way, like a museum curator

A. R. preferred A. My grandma has things from when she was little. If I broke one, I'd talk quiet like Kit in A.
L. M. preferred B. When I'm in trouble I talk too fast and laugh, like Kit in B. That felt real to me.
S. T. preferred A for the ending, B for the start. B was funnier at first, but when she asked if Kit got hurt, I wanted the sad music.
Tap Play again with one switch changed. Watch the first five lines, then tap Stop and rate the change.
Play the first five lines before stopping. Tap Play to try your comparison again.
That was your base version. Flip one switch, then tap Play to compare its effect.

Kit A.style: Say quietly and slowly, a little shaky, like a scared kid owning up

Kit B.style: Say fast and too loud with a nervous laugh, like a kid trying to make it no big deal

Holloway A.style: Say softly and slowly, like a kind old neighbor who is sad but gentle

Holloway B.style: Say briskly and surprised, like a busy gardener who just heard odd news

scene_lines: Kit! Did you bring my bike back?
The chain came off on the big hill. And then the wheel... bent.
Oh. I rode that bike when I was your age.
I'm sorry. I'll fix it. I'll save my allowance. I'll...
Then come in. We'll look at that wheel together.
